newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods--Doldrums empower talk over action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods--Doldrums empower talk over action.

text.p: The U.S. cash refined oil products market, entrenched for weeks in summer doldrums, saw activity slow to a near-standstill and differentials talked at stable levels Friday amid the approach of the weekend.
July NYMEX gasoline rose 0.26 cent at 1230 EDT (1630 GMT) to 57.05 cents a gallon, while August NYMEX gained 0.29 cent to 56.75 cents.
July and August heating oil both jumped 0.68 cent, to 52.70 cents and 52.90 cents, respectively.
U.S. GULF COAST

Regular unleaded gasoline appeared to be settling down for a typically slow Friday session after a volatile session on Thursday saw the then-prompt cycle's scheduling deadline on the Colonial Pipeline expire with characteristic volatility.

"Majors got the party going and they killed it," said one gasoline trader, referring to the way cash differentials firmed early in Thursday's session only to retreat back to softer levels all on the buying and selling moves of majors.

Prompt "M1" regular unleaded conventional gasoline was talked Friday morning at around 3.10 cents under July NYMEX unleaded futures, with any-month barrels notionally pegged at 3.50 cents under and possibly even weaker.
Premium "V1" grade was steady, with offers on prompt material at 5.00 cents over prompt M1, traders said.

Differentials on the distillates were also steady to a touch firmer, with prompt 86-grade heating oil offered at 2.25 cents under July NYMEX heating oil, and 74-grade low sulphur diesel talked at between 2.00 and 1.75 cents under July NYMEX.
NEW YORK HARBOR
NYH differentials held true to their recent rangebound pattern, with hardly a flicker of activity.
"It's Friday and I don't see any deals getting done," one bored New York player said.

Prompt "M2" conventional unleaded gasoline was offered at 3.0 cents below July futures, stable with Thursday diffs, while offers on "A2" reformulated edged a bit higher to 0.25 cents below the July NYMEX print.
On the distillate side, NYH heating oil offers were stable at 0.20 cent below July futures and low sulfur diesel steady at a half cent over, traders said.
MIDCONTINENT

Unleaded gasoline differentials weakened amid a lack of demand and a rise in NYMEX futures. Group Three unleaded was down a half cent at 3.50/4.00 cents over July NYMEX. First cycle July was done at 3.25 cents over the print, traders said.
Chicago prompt unleaded, for July delivery, was down a quarter cent at 0.50/0.75 cent over the August screen, traders said.
"It's very quiet and hardly any demand," said a Group Three broker.
Meanwhile, low sulphur continued taking a step down amid ample supply. Prompt Group Three material was done at 1.00 cent over July heating oil, brokers said.
--New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
